This is the default configuration for Tiny Tapeout projects. It should fit most designs.
If you change it, please make sure you understand what you are doing. We are not responsible
if your project fails because of a bad configuration.
!!! DO NOT EDIT THIS FILE unless you know what you are doing !!!
If you get stuck with this config, please open an issue or get in touch via the discord.
Here are some of the variables you may want to change:
PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT - You can increase this if Global Placement fails with error GPL-0302.
Users have reported that values up to 80 worked well for them.
CLOCK_PERIOD - Increase this in case you are getting setup time violations.
The value is in nanoseconds, so 20ns == 50MHz.
Hold slack margin - Increase them in case you are getting hold violations.
RUN_LINTER, LINTER_INCLUDE_PDK_MODELS - Disabling the linter is not recommended!
If you need a custom clock configuration, read the following documentation first:
https://tinytapeout.com/faq/#how-can-i-map-an-additional-external-clock-to-one-of-the-gpios
Configuration docs: https://librelane.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/configuration.html
JS-ASIC changes for the SRAM program memory (src/prog_mem.v). Everything else in
this file is the ihp-cmos5l template, except FP_PDN_VPITCH/FP_PDN_VOFFSET below.
Follows the working integration in 2AMLogic/sg13cmos5l-protocol-emulator (Apache-2.0).
Two RM_IHPSG13_1P_256x16 macros (236.8 x 118.78 um each) side by side, mid-height,
right of the pin cluster (Tiny Tapeout pins sit on the top edge at x < 192 um). The
x positions are 91.2 + k*44.96 um so the strap lattice lines up (see src/pdn_cfg.tcl).
The flow reads the macro's LEF/GDS/liberty from the PDK; flow/ holds the blackbox
that the Verilator lint step needs.
Three supply pins per macro: VDD!, VSS! and the bit-array supply VDDARRAY!.
An unconnected VDDARRAY! powers up but never retains a bit.
The macro's power pins are Metal4-only and TopMetal1 is not on the precheck's CMOS5L
layer allowlist, so the default PDN script cannot connect them. This one draws Metal4
bridges on the macro's own stripes and makes full-height VPWR/VGND pins.
Magic DRC is informational here; sign-off is the precheck's KLayout deck (the PDK's
magic README: magic for interactive work, klayout for final sign-off). Read without
flattening, the SRAM GDS gives ~29k Magic errors per macro, all inside the macro (run
41910413971). The PDK's libs.tech/magic/read_sram_gds.tcl flattens these cells because
they are ambiguous to magic; MAGIC_GDS_FLATGLOB applies the same list. It only affects
the Magic.DRC step, not the GDS that is streamed out.
Slew and load into the macros. Hold fixing (after CTS) puts weak delay cells on the
address and data nets, and one driver feeds the same pin on both macros. Run cc3339f
had 18 max-slew violations (A_REN 1.31 ns vs a 0.595 ns limit) and 3 max-cap ones on
A_DOUT. Design repair after global routing re-buffers those nets with the hold cells in
place and real wire loads. The two *_CORNERS lists make any slew or cap violation fail
the flow; the default [""] matches no corner and only warns.
Buffer every net longer than 120 um. One driver feeds the same pin on both macros, ~270 um
apart, and run de24585 still failed max slew (A_REN 1.31 ns vs 0.595) and max cap on A_DOUT.
The same setting cleared the last violations in the SRAM experiments (run 41994812789).

JS-ASIC: template pitch 50.0 would short core straps against the SRAM macros'
opposite-net stripes. 44.96 = 4 x the macro's 11.24 um stripe pitch; the offset puts
each crossing strap on a same-net stripe or in clear space (src/pdn_cfg.tcl).
